Ratio Calculator

Reduce a two-part ratio to its simplest whole-number terms and scale it to a requested total. How to use this calculator

  1. Enter first ratio part, second ratio part, total to split.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How ratio is calculated

For positive parts a:b, divide both by gcd(a,b). Given a total T, the first share is T×a/(a+b) and the second is T×b/(a+b). A 2:3 mixture totaling 20 units contains 8 units of the first part and 12 of the second.

Simplify a:b by gcd(a,b); split total T into Ta/(a+b) and Tb/(a+b).
A worked example

A 2:3 mixture totaling 20 units contains 8 units of the first part and 12 of the second.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Does 2:3 mean two divided by three?

It describes relative quantities; its value as a fraction is 2/3.

Can one part be zero?

Yes; the output still describes the resulting split, provided both parts are not zero.
